title: ¿Por qué los pájaros pueden pararse en los cables eléctricos? 🐦
staging_mode_proposal: world: a street at dusk modelled as an environment (sky gradient, a row of poles, three wires in catenary curves, a rooftop line), the camera travelling along the wire with the current. First `world` production: its environment is measured first (format policy 'Staging mode', proof P3).
curiosity_reason: Seen daily in every city of every country; the insulating-feet explanation is the one everyone gives.
hook_question: ¿Por qué los pájaros pueden pararse en los cables eléctricos sin electrocutarse?
false_belief: Sus patas los aíslan de la electricidad.
turn: Scene 5: a bird that touches two things at once, the wire and the pole, opens a path through its body, which is why big birds are the ones electrocuted.
closing_reframe: Al pájaro no lo salvan sus patas: lo salva tocar un solo cable.
share_archetype: ese amigo que cambia un enchufe sin cortar la luz
engine_reason: code3d on the asset route (engine selection: rigid poles and wires, energy graphics): the bird is the library asset bird (open job, perched pose sealed before production); poles, wires and the street are geometric world builds; the current is emissive accent pulses.
description:
¿Por qué los pájaros pueden pararse en los cables eléctricos? Porque sus dos patas están en el mismo cable, al mismo voltaje.
Si tocan el cable y el poste a la vez, la corriente sí los cruza. 🐦
Envíaselo a ese amigo que cambia un enchufe sin cortar la luz.

scenes.name: hook
scenes.narration: ¿Por qué los pájaros pueden pararse en los cables eléctricos sin electrocutarse? Casi todos creen que sus patas los aíslan de la electricidad.
scenes.what_changes: A street at dusk: a small bird glides in and lands on the middle wire between two poles; the wire bounces under it; the tag ¿PATAS AISLANTES? appears by its feet.
scenes.transformation: cable vacío → un pájaro aterriza encima
scenes.camera: seguimiento del pájaro en vuelo hasta que se posa, y acercamiento a las patas

elements.name: a small bird perched on a power line
elements.route: library bird (open job; perched-on-a-wire state) on a geometric wire between poles
elements.risk: medium-high: the hero is an unsealed asset; the wire and poles are the context cue; proof P1

scenes.name: viaje
scenes.narration: Sigamos a la electricidad. Viaja por el cobre del cable, empujada por la diferencia de voltaje entre un extremo de la línea y el otro.
scenes.what_changes: The camera drops onto the wire far down the line: accent pulses race along the copper toward the bird, passing pole after pole; at the far end of the line a high glow, at the other a low one.
scenes.transformation: cable apagado → pulsos de corriente que corren por él hacia el pájaro
scenes.camera: travelling rasante a lo largo del cable, acompañando los pulsos

elements.name: electric current flowing along a power line
elements.route: emissive accent pulses travelling inside a semi-transparent wire jacket; poles in frame
elements.risk: medium-high: readers may name only 'power lines'; the pulses are the event; proof P2

scenes.name: patas
scenes.narration: Al llegar al pájaro, podría desviarse: subir por una pata, cruzar su cuerpo y bajar por la otra.
scenes.what_changes: The pulses reach the bird's feet and slow; a dotted ghost path draws up one leg, through the body and down the other leg, as if offering the current a detour.
scenes.transformation: corriente bajo las patas → aparece el posible desvío por el cuerpo del pájaro
scenes.camera: empuje a las patas y subida por el cuerpo del pájaro

elements.name: bird on a wire with a dotted path through its legs and body
elements.route: bird asset + dotted accent curve; the bird stays in its sealed perched state
elements.risk: medium: proof P1 covers the bird on the wire; the dotted path is an annotation

scenes.name: mismo
scenes.narration: Pero no lo hace: sus dos patas están en el mismo cable, al mismo voltaje. Sin diferencia entre ellas, nada empuja la corriente por el pájaro, y sigue de largo por el cobre.
scenes.what_changes: Both feet light in the same accent shade; the ghost path fades out; the pulses pass under the feet without slowing and race on down the line; the bird preens, unbothered.
scenes.transformation: posible desvío → la corriente pasa de largo bajo las patas
scenes.camera: travelling lateral que deja al pájaro atrás siguiendo los pulsos
overlays_plan: label = between the two feet at 'mismo'

elements.name: current passing under a bird on a wire
elements.route: same staging as P2 with the bird in frame

scenes.name: poste
scenes.narration: El peligro es tocar dos cosas a la vez, como el cable y el poste. Ahí sí hay diferencia, y la corriente cruza el cuerpo. Por eso las aves grandes, que alcanzan con las alas, son las que más mueren electrocutadas.
scenes.what_changes: The turn: the camera pulls back along the whole line to a pole top; a large bird lands on the crossarm and spreads its wings, one wingtip touching the wire; a red path lights from the wire through the wing and body down into the pole; an error-red X closes over it before anything else happens.
scenes.transformation: pájaro chico a salvo → un ave grande toca cable y poste y la corriente la cruza
scenes.camera: retroceso a lo largo de toda la línea hasta lo alto del poste

elements.name: a large bird with spread wings on a power pole
elements.route: library bird (flying, wings spread state, scaled up) on a geometric pole crossarm; red emissive path
elements.risk: high: a scaled songbird may not read as a large bird; the pole and wire are the cue; proof P4

scenes.name: cierre
scenes.narration: Así que al pájaro no lo salvan sus patas: lo salva tocar un solo cable. Envíaselo a ese amigo que cambia un enchufe sin cortar la luz.
scenes.what_changes: Single reframe image: back on the middle wire, the small bird sits with both feet lit the same shade while the pulses stream under it; the camera rises to show the whole street of poles and wires, every bird on a single wire.
scenes.transformation: un pájaro en el cable → la calle entera con pájaros a salvo en sus cables
scenes.camera: subida desde el pájaro hasta la calle entera

sources: Mechanism: a bird on one wire has both feet at essentially the same potential, so there is no voltage across its body and no current through it; the current stays in the conductor. Danger comes when the body bridges two points at different potential (two conductors, or a conductor and a grounded pole). Indiana Public Media 'A Moment of Science: Bird on a wire'; MIT Alumni Association explainer (live search 2026-11-11). FLAGGED: add one utility or textbook reference at the beat sheet.

Large birds (raptors: eagles, hawks, owls) are the ones most often electrocuted, because their wingspan can bridge a conductor and a pole or two conductors; utilities fit raptor-safe poles. SciShow summary (live search 2026-11-11). FLAGGED: cite the Avian Power Line Interaction Committee (APLIC), 'Suggested Practices for Avian Protection on Power Lines' (2006), at the beat sheet; if it cannot be read, scene 5's last sentence becomes 'Por eso las aves grandes corren más peligro', with the same staging.
No number is spoken or rendered in this script.
simplifications: Current is drawn as pulses moving along the wire; the electrons drift slowly and the energy travels in the field. The 'detour' path is an annotation, not a physical path that current 'tries'.
Both feet are shown at exactly the same potential; in reality the short stretch of wire between them has a tiny voltage drop, far too small to matter.
The pole is shown as grounded wood/metal for clarity; real crossarm hardware varies.
flatness_test: 1. hook: a bird lands on an empty wire.
2. viaje: current pulses race along the wire toward the bird.
3. patas: the pulses reach the feet and a dotted detour through the bird appears.
4. mismo: both feet light the same shade, the detour fades and the pulses pass under the bird.
5. poste: a large bird on the pole spreads its wings onto the wire and a red path crosses its body (turn).
6. cierre: the whole street, every bird safe on a single wire.
